note: Record of a corrected row-count field in four excitation dataset summaries. The datasets live outside the repo, so without this file the repair is visible only to whoever opens the JSON -- and the reason the undercount mattered is that plausible numbers propagate unchallenged.
cause: The collector emitted `rows` as kept * WINDOW_ROWS. WINDOW_ROWS is the BURST length, not the episode length; an episode is WINDOW_ROWS*bursts + recover_rows*(bursts-1) rows. With bursts>1 the field undercounts by roughly the burst count.
why_it_survived: The same substitution also produced a printed line reading 'first tip at row median 332 of 10', which is self-evidently absurd and was caught in minutes. The JSON field was plausible, so nothing flagged it.
fix: Both the JSON field and the printed line now derive from a rows_written accumulator incremented where rows are actually written, rather than recomputed from a formula that can drift from the loop. Landed in scripts/collection/collect_go2_excitation.py.
repair_method: Recounted from each windows.csv (line count minus header). The on-disk JSONs each carry a `rows_field_repaired` string preserving the old value; no value was silently overwritten.
